text:
Michelle: Heads-up — Tenant A is spiking and a bunch of inference pods are queueing against the hosted GPU pool. Frontend traces show increased latency for their routes.
Raj: Is this scheduler saturation or just batching backlog? Any evictions? :eyes:
Dina: Looking at the scheduler events — pods are Pending with "no nodes available" for the last 7m. We have a mix: some namespaces are marked dedicated but don't have the correct tolerations/annotations, so they fall through to hosted fallback.
Raj: Oof. So the routing config is correct but the pod spec doesn't guarantee placement onto dedicated nodepools.
Leo: I dug in — autoscaler did scale up a hosted-preemptible pool, but dedicated pools had taints missing on a couple nodepools in us-west1. Taints + tolerations mismatch = scheduling failure.
Infra-bot: [autoscaler] scaled up 4 nodes in us-west1-gpu-preemptible at 2025-06-12T14:12Z (event id: a3f9e)
sre-ops: kube-scheduler excerpt: "Predicate failed: MatchToleration: no matching taints on any node for pod infer-worker-xyz"
Dina: Paste of failing pod manifest for context:
```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: infer-worker
  labels:
    tenant: tenant-a
  annotations:
    redwood/route-preference: dedicated
spec:
  tolerations:
  - key: "dedicated-gpu"
    operator: "Equal"
    value: "true"
    effect: "NoSchedule"
```
Raj: Actionable steps I'm proposing: 1) validate nodepool taints for all dedicated pools (scriptable), 2) run a quick job to reconcile missing pod tolerations for affected namespaces, 3) change fallback window from indefinite to 180s then billing-tag fallback.
Olivia: We have to weigh cost — if we force strict dedicated routing, Tenant A will push more reserved capacity requests. Preliminary calc: strict isolation ~2.3x per-token infra cost vs hosted bursting. Need a soft option.
Dina: Proposal: introduce `redwood/isolation=soft` label on namespace. Behavior: scheduling prefers dedicated (taint+toleration), but after X seconds (configurable) a fallback route is allowed with a billing flag `fallback:dedicated-to-hosted` so we can attribute cost.
Michelle: Ops runbook update request: add checklist — 1) check autoscaler events, 2) check nodepool taints, 3) check kube-scheduler logs for MatchToleration failures, 4) if >5m and still Pending, escalate to infra oncall.
Leo: I'll open an RFC and a small reconciler to ensure namespaces have either the strict or soft label, and a one-off Job to patch existing deployments. I'll also add unit tests for the rollover timer.
Raj: Can we also add an alert: "PodPendingBecauseNoDedicatedNode" with a burn rate 5m? That would catch this earlier.
sre-ops: +1 for the alert. Also recommend we emit an event metric that includes `tenant` label so billing can ingest.
Infra-bot: Created issue INFRA-834: validate-taints-and-soft-isolate-feature-toggle (assigned Leo) :thumbsup:
Michelle: Thanks — please post the RFC link here when ready and tag oncall for validation during rollout.
